cases.question: According to the ArabicMMLU abstract, how many tasks, questions, and evaluated models are reported, and what score did the best Arabic-centric model achieve? Cite each number.

references.text:
Our data comprises 40 tasks
and 14,575 multiple-choice questions in Mod-
ern Standard Arabic (MSA) and is carefully
constructed by collaborating with native speak-
ers in the region. Our comprehensive evalu-
ations of 35 models reveal substantial room
for improvement, particularly among the best
open-source models. Notably, BLOOMZ, mT0,
LLaMA2, and Falcon struggle to achieve a
score of 50%, while even the top-performing
Arabic-centric model only achieves a score of
62.3%.

cases.question: According to the ArabicNumBench abstract, how many models, providers, and individual test cases were evaluated? Compare few-shot chain-of-thought accuracy with zero-shot accuracy, using the reported numbers.

references.text:
We evaluate
71 models from 10 providers using four prompting strategies
(zero-shot, zero-shot CoT, few-shot, few-shot CoT) on 210 number
reading tasks spanning six contextual categories: pure numer-
als, addresses, dates, quantities, and prices. Our evaluation
comprises 59,010 individual test cases and tracks extraction
methods to measure structured output generation. Evaluation
reveals substantial performance variation, with accuracy ranging
from 14.29% to 99.05% across models and strategies. Few-
shot Chain-of-Thought prompting achieves 2.8x higher accuracy
than zero-shot approaches (80.06% vs 28.76%).
